findings.detail: The problem repeats the earlier questions M2-S49-T2 and M3-S13-T2. In each, the team must design how a verification pass routes limited human reviewer attention. The correct action is the same: per-finding confidence, thresholds calibrated on a labeled validation set, and low-confidence items routed to reviewers. Only the setting changes, from extraction to CI review, so the same reasoning leads to option B. A different problem is needed, for example a cause, a different failure, or a choice between two rules.

blind_answer.reason: A verification pass that attaches a confidence level to each finding, with thresholds calibrated on a labeled validation set, lets the pipeline route only the uncertain findings to the maintainers (4.6-S3, 5.5-S3). That cuts their workload while still screening out false positives. A only speeds up scanning, so the maintainers still read everything. C still sends every finding to them. D adds latency to blocking reviews and does nothing to lower the volume.
